problem: I'm writing a little notes-and-tasks service in Jac that I'll serve with `jac start`. I want each logged-in user's tasks to live on their own private root, so creation should go through a private walker that lands on the authenticated user's root automatically. Show me the create side: spawn it twice and then list what landed under root.

For my task service I want a listing endpoint that returns every todo as one JSON array rather than a stream of partial results: collect during the walk and send everything back in a single report at the end, marked private so each user only ever sees their own graph. Seed a few todos in an entry block so the file also runs standalone.

My task app needs an edit endpoint. Clients only keep the id that creation reported back, so write a private walker that takes a jid string plus new title and done values, walks the caller's root until the jid matches, mutates the node in place, and stops early. A bogus id should simply produce no report.

The last piece of my task service CRUD set is delete. Write a private walker that carries the target id, traverses the user's root, and deletes the node right where it stands when the jid matches. I don't want to clean up edges manually -- deleting should detach connections by itself.

I'm building a project tracker where deleting a project must take its tasks with it -- orphaned children would rot the graph. The catch is that deleting mid-traversal detaches the very edges I need to reach those children. Show me how to collect the whole subtree first and remove it in one pass at the end, printing the board before and after.

In my social mini-app friendships are typed Friend edges, and unfriending must drop exactly one relationship without touching either person node. Some pairs also carry Coworker edges that have to survive. Pin the edge by both endpoints, delete the edge objects, and show the coworker link stayed intact.

I'm prototyping an event page in Jac and want a guestbook that works over HTTP without me writing route handlers. Two public walkers: one signs the guestbook, one reads the latest entries. Over `jac start` the walker fields should become the request body and the reports the response -- but keep an entry block so it runs standalone too.

For my reading-club site I want an anonymous poll -- no login, just tap a book title. One public walker sets up the options, another records a vote against a counter node, and a third reports tallies as the response. Simulate a few clicks locally so the file works without a server.

My micro-blog needs a public feed: whoever calls publish, authenticated or not, hangs their post on the shared public graph and opens that single post to readers while ownership stays theirs. Use the shared root reachable from any request context and arm a read-level grant on each fresh post. Have the program print both the shared root's id and the current root's id so I can see they match on a plain CLI run.

This is the reader half of my micro-blog: any caller, even anonymous, lists posts off the shared public graph in creation order. No auth needed since the commons floor lets everyone reach it and authors grant their posts readable. Include the publisher walker so the file runs standalone.

My journal app keeps notes closed on the owner's root by default, and I need a share-link feature. The owner arms a per-instance grant on one note giving everyone exactly READ -- not connect, not write -- while the rest of the graph stays sealed. Print the ambient access levels and verify the shared note is readable afterward.

The share-link in my journal app needs an off switch. Show a walker that arms a READ grant on a note and another call that revokes it, returning the node to owner-only. Track a flag on the note itself so the transition shows in the output.

My app keeps a docs cache that anyone may rebuild; openness here is an invariant of the type rather than a per-instance choice. Encode that once on the archetype with an access hook so every instance is open at WRITE level to every user, subtypes included. Pair it with an open edge type too, since edges are checked separately.

For my reports module the rule is: published reports are world-readable, unpublished ones fall back to whatever per-instance grants say. Define the archetype hook to return a READ level when published and None otherwise, so drafts stay closable but owners can still share them selectively. Add a publish walker that flips the flag and drops the now-redundant grant.

I want a dashboard endpoint for my task app: total, completed, pending, completion rate, and story points burned versus planned. Accumulate counters during traversal and report one dict at Root exit so the response stays clean. Guard division by zero for accounts with no todos yet.

My recipe box needs search that feels ranked, not just filtered. Score each substring match by where the query appears -- recipe name beats cuisine beats ingredient, plus a small bonus for shorter names -- then sort best-first before reporting. Show the sorted hits for a query like 'curry'.

While debugging my app's graph I kept wanting a quick look at what's actually stored. Build a small IOU ledger, print each node's unique id, explicitly persist the nodes, flush pending changes, and dump the structure from the root. Keep it small enough that the dump is readable.

I wanted to understand how multi-user data lays out in storage. Enumerate every root in the deployment, count each root's direct children by type, and check whether there really is only one root outside a served environment. Print a line about what this layout would look like under `jac start` -- one root per user plus the shared root.

I'm writing a small blogging service in Jac. Authors keep unpublished drafts private on their own root; publishing moves the text onto the shared public graph where even anonymous readers can list articles and leave comments; deleting an article removes its comments too. Give me the whole thing: public feed, article view, and comment endpoints, private draft tools, and cascade deletion -- runnable standalone and under `jac start`.

For my team I want a shared task board in Jac. The board itself is open structure teammates can attach to, encoded once as an archetype policy instead of remembered grants; tasks are user-owned contributions armed readable as they're created. Add a full private CRUD set plus a stats walker reporting totals, completion rate, and per-assignee counts in a single response.
